target_customer: Brands paying for virtual influencer and character campaigns early on, later writers paying for an AI long form writing tool (Plotdrive)
problem: Creators and brands lacked tools to build and perform persistent fictional characters and stories; later, long form writers needed AI help finishing manuscripts.
business_model: Brand partnerships for virtual characters, later subscription software for writers
product_category: Virtual influencers, narrative games and AI storytelling tools

founders.name: Jay Rosenkrantz
previous_startups: One of the earliest poker training platforms (name and outcome not given)
founders.background_notes: Former professional high stakes poker player turned company builder, per the YC founder bio. Later co-founded Heroic Story with his brother (The Block, 2022).

founders.name: Scott Rosenkrantz
founders.background_notes: YC bio cites about seven years of 0 to 1 product and go to market work and growing Plotdrive to hundreds of paying customers.

competitors.name: Brud (Lil Miquela)
competitors.what: Virtual influencer character Lil Miquela used in brand campaigns
competitors.traction_then: Brand campaigns and a CNN profile in June 2018
competitors.funding_then: Reported around 6 million dollars in April 2018 from Sequoia Capital, BoxGroup and SV Angel

technical_complexity.rationale: Real time character animation, virtual production tooling and games are standard but demanding engineering for two people; the later LLM writing engine relied on third party models.

defensibility.rationale: Characters and narrative tools were easy to copy; no network effect or proprietary data is described.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Brud was acquired by Dapper Labs in 2021 per Sequoia; large platforms later added AI writing features, which affected Plotdrive's space.

market_need_then: Brands were testing virtual influencers in 2018 and 2019 (Brud funding and press), and Figments reported early brand partnerships with Reebok and Guayaki in a 2020 YC talk.

identity.mascot_or_character: Virtual characters were the product itself; none named in sources
identity.voice_and_tone: Reflective, as in the closing statement about technological inflection points

rebrands.why: Product focus moved to an AI writing engine; YC lists Plotdrive as a separate company page

brand_strength.rationale: A YC talk and a few brand deals only; no press on the brand itself was found, and a web search returned generic virtual influencer articles.

pivots.to: AI characters, creative tools and the Plotdrive AI writing engine
pivots.why: The company's own summary lists a sequence of products over seven years; no dates or reasons are given

outcome_analysis: Figments joined YC in Summer 2019 with virtual influencers and spent seven years moving through narrative games, AI characters, creative tools and finally Plotdrive, an AI writing engine that reportedly reached hundreds of paying customers. YC marks Figments inactive while a separate Plotdrive page is active, and the founders went on to Heroic Story. The reason it stopped is not public, so failure factors stay empty.
notes: plotdrive.com returned HTTP 503. The 125K seed is from Dealroom's Plotdrive page and rests on a single database; it may belong to the Plotdrive entity rather than Figments, and has no date. Search showed Plotdrive YC page as active with team size 4. Brud was founded before the batch; its TechCrunch article is dated April 2018. Education of both founders is not given on the YC page.
